newsitem.title: USA: DOE sees Calif. Elk Hills crude sold by late Wed.
newsitem.headline: DOE sees Calif. Elk Hills crude sold by late Wed.

text.p: The U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) said Monday it still offered crude oil from last week's auction at the Elk Hills Naval Petroleum Reserve in Tupman, Calif. and hoped to complete sales by Wednesday.
Around 5,075 barrels per day (bpd) of light crude remains to be sold following lower-than-normal interest in last week's auction.
A DOE official said he was calling back the original bidders to see who would be willing to pay the highest by tomorrow.
"I hope (sales are) wrapped up by this time tomorrow," a DOE official said Monday.
Last Thursday, the DOE received bids for 11,025 barrels of the available 16,100 bpd offered by the government, a low level of demand, according to a DOE official.
The average bid last week stood at $2.79 a barrel under the DOE's base reference price of $21.18.
The DOE attributed weak demand to heavy volumes of light sweet crude imports, which are forcing more local crude, like Elk Hills grades, into storage.
"There's more oil coming in than people need," the official said.
